rv.q: The show, which remains a zesty and full-bodied original, began life in fact as a participant in the New York Fringe Festival, and given its toilet-centric plot, it was a reasonable level of entry.

I am relieved—even a little surprised—to report that the show, which opened last night at the Henry Miller, still manages to be both escapist and nasty fun, frivolous yet pertinent, and fills a bit of the darkness with elevated foolishness of a very high order.
Yet it is still the same superb production with a terrific cast and an adventurous score that sounds better the second time around.
That winking tone grows monotonous quickly — it's hard to muster sustained interest in a cast of characters stalking the stage with ironic quotation marks around their ears.

It's alive and well and living in Urinetown—the show that gives New York a chance to laugh and to heal at the same time.
